People: Charles Baudelaire (author, Wikidata Q501), died 1867; Auguste Poulet-Malassis (editor, Wikidata Q328607), died 1878; Félicien Rops (illustrator, Wikidata Q378129), died 1898. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Baudelaire, Charles, 1821-1867; Poulet-Malassis, Auguste, 1825-1878 [Editor]; Rops, Félicien, 1833-1898 [Illustrator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: Les épaves / de Charles Baudelaire ; avec une eau-forte frontispice de Félicien Rops, À l'enseigne du Coq (Amsterdam), 1866, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/bnf-bpt6k1054576n. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 94%, 80%, 75% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Auguste Poulet-Malassis, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
